claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 exhibits a reported hierarchical heterostructure.
A predictive framework can fuse microscopy- and diffraction-derived microstructural descriptors with machine learning.
The machine-learning model will be trained on a subset of simulation and experimental data.
Grain boundaries, phase distributions, and substructural characteristics mediate the mechanical response of HfNbTiVAl10.
Direct microstructural descriptors can capture the heterogeneous hierarchical nature of the alloy.
Combining microstructural descriptors with data-driven learning can approximate the interplay of features governing elastic deformation.
Combining microstructural descriptors with data-driven learning can approximate the interplay of features governing plastic deformation.
Combining microstructural descriptors with data-driven learning can approximate crack-initiation and crack-propagation behavior.
The hybrid framework will be more computationally efficient than traditional physics-based simulations.
The hybrid framework will predict Young's modulus more accurately than traditional physics-based simulations.
The hybrid framework will predict yield strength more accurately than traditional physics-based simulations.
The hybrid framework will predict fracture-related behavior more accurately than traditional physics-based simulations.
Predicted Young's modulus will be within ±5% of the experimental value.
Predicted yield strength will be within ±5% of the experimental value.
Predicted fracture toughness will be within ±5% of the experimental value.
The hybrid framework will reduce computation time by at least 40% relative to established simulations.
Poorly resolved or inaccurately characterized hierarchical features may cause the approach to fail.
High strain rates or temperatures may cause failure when they introduce behavior or phase transitions absent from the training data.
Predictive performance depends on microstructural-data quality and training-set representativeness.
Failure to attain either ±5% predictive error or a 40% computation-time reduction will falsify the hypothesis.
